title: Regular base change of the prime-power closed-immersion Gysin classes and the regular pinnings
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Work on small etale $D^+$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] with the roots-of-unity twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] between Noetherian regular affine schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme]; its ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence (each generator acts injectively modulo its predecessors), whose length is the locally constant codimension $c$. Write
$$\operatorname{Cl}_i:\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]\xrightarrow{\sim}i^!\Lambda_T$$
for the Gysin isomorphism of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] for $i$ (virtual relative dimension $d_i=-c$); for a closed immersion, the right adjoint $i^!$ of $Ri_!=i_*$ is the derived closed-support functor of [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel].

Regular base change. Let $r:T'\to T$ be a regular morphism with $T'$ a Noetherian affine scheme: $r$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and its fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] remain regular after every finite extension of the residue field. Put $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, with $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $r':Z'\to Z$. Then $T'$ and $Z'$ are regular, the ideal of $i'$ is locally generated by the pulled-back regular sequence, so $i'$ has codimension $c\circ r'$, and under the canonical exchange isomorphism $r'^*i^!\Lambda_T\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^!r^*\Lambda_T=i'^!\Lambda_{T'}$ of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change], with $r'^*(\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c])=\Lambda_{Z'}(-c\circ r')[-2c\circ r']$, one has $r'^*(\operatorname{Cl}_i)=\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}$.

Regular pinnings. If moreover $T$ is connected and excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], then for every $x\in T$, with $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,x}$ of codimension $\dim\mathcal O_{T,x}$, the canonical pinning of $\Lambda_T$ at $x$ in [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit] is $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}$, and the pinning of $\Lambda_T(m)[2m]$ at $x$ there is $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}(m)[2m]$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Proposition 2.2.3.1 (base change of the generalized classes) and Definition 2.3.1 (regular-immersion class from the conormal bundle); Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.1.1 (inverse-class pinning on regular schemes) and Lemma 4.3.1.2 (use of the base-change compatibility f^*(Cl_x) = Cl_F).

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $T'=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $S$ flat over $R$. The fibre rings are regular by the regular-morphism hypothesis (take the identity residue-field extension), so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-map-ascent] makes $S$ regular. The quotient map $R\to R/I$ is finite type: its algebra is generated by the empty set. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change] applies to the regular ring map $R\to S$ and gives a regular map $R/I\to S/IS$. The latter ring is Noetherian as a quotient of $S$. Since $R/I$ is regular by the hypothesis on $Z$, a second application of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-map-ascent] proves $Z'$ regular. This uses base change by the finite-type quotient only, not an unrestricted field-extension permanence assertion.

source.place: Tag 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change); algebra.tex Tag 031E (lemma-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre), applied to the local rings at every target prime

proof.text: Since $Z$ and $T$ are regular Noetherian, [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] makes $i$ a regular closed immersion, with locally constant codimension $c$ equal to the length of a local regular generating sequence, as the statement asserts; the same node says regular immersions and their codimensions are preserved by flat base change, which the following argument makes explicit. On a chart with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ put $I_j=(f_1,\ldots,f_j)$. Tensor the injections $R/I_{j-1}\xrightarrow{f_j}R/I_{j-1}$ with the flat $R$-algebra of any affine chart upstairs. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] the resulting multiplication by the image of $f_j$ on $S/I_{j-1}S$ is injective. At a point of $Z'$ the final quotient is nonzero, because its defining ideal lies in the point's prime. Hence this is a regular sequence there and defines the pulled-back immersion. Its length is the original $c$, so the locally defined codimension is $c\circ r'$. Equivalently the conormal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-flat-base-change] is invertible, and its source has rank $c$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free]; therefore the conormal rank has not changed. If a component of the pullback is empty there is no point on which a codimension needs to be evaluated. All these assertions are local on the indicated affine charts.

source.place: Tag 0473 (lemma-conormal-functorial-flat); flat tensor exactness and regular-sequence conormal basis

proof.text: On such a chart form $X_j=V(f_1,\ldots,f_j)$ in $X_0=T$ and its pullback $X'_j$. Each inclusion $a_j:X_j\hookrightarrow X_{j-1}$ and $a'_j:X'_j\hookrightarrow X'_{j-1}$ is Cartier by Step 2. For $A=\Lambda$ and $N=\ell^n$, [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] gives $r_{j-1}^*k_j=k'_j$ under its canonical closed exchange. The equality holds for every one of these divisor squares; regularity of intermediate $X_j$ is unnecessary. Set $C_i:Ri_*\Lambda_Z\to\Lambda_T(c)[2c]$ to be the adjoint supported class of $\eta_{i,n}$, and expand its Cartier-flag composite using [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus]. Pullback is a functor, so it sends each composition to the composition of its pullbacks. Substitute the displayed equalities, starting with $k_c$ and proceeding outwards to $k_1$. The canonical direct-image comparisons compose, and the twist comparisons compose by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The resulting composite is exactly the primed nested composite, hence $r^*C_i=C_{i'}$. This argument uses finite prime-power coefficients directly, not reduction of a class modulo $\ell$.

source.place: XVI Theorem 2.3.2 and Proposition 2.2.3.1, applied to a local Cartier flag

proof.text:
Set $L=\Lambda_Z(-c)[-2c]$ and $L'=r'^*L$. The signed twist pullback is $L'=\Lambda_{Z'}(-c\circ r')[-2c\circ r']$ by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Let $\epsilon_i:i_*i^!\to1$ be the closed counit. The adjoint of $\operatorname{Cl}_i$ is $\epsilon_i\circ i_*\operatorname{Cl}_i:i_*L\to\Lambda_T$; this is $C_i$ with $(c)[2c]$ cancelled. Indeed, [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] defines the regular-immersion class, and the Gysin isomorphism of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] is this same class from ILO XVI Definition 2.3.1, with the twist and shift cancelled. Let $\beta:r'^*i^!\to i'^!r^*$ be the exchange of [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change]. Its counit compatibility gives
$$\epsilon_{i'}\circ i'_*\beta\circ i'_*r'^*\operatorname{Cl}_i=r^*(\epsilon_i\circ i_*\operatorname{Cl}_i).$$
Step 3 identifies the right side with $\epsilon_{i'}\circ i'_*\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}$. The adjunction bijection on morphisms therefore gives $\beta\circ r'^*\operatorname{Cl}_i=\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}$. The cited exchange is invertible because $r$ is regular; [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] makes both classes invertible because the two pairs are regular affine by Step 1. This proves equality of the specified maps, with the canonical exchange, rather than just existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.3.1, XVII Corollary 4.2.3 and Lemma 4.3.1.2

proof.text: The local equalities give a global equality on $Z'$. Indeed, compose each side of Step 4 with $\operatorname{Cl}_{i'}^{-1}$. This turns both maps into endomorphisms of $L'$. On every stratum where $c\circ r'$ is constant, cancel its invertible twist and shift, using [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The endomorphisms become maps $\Lambda_{Z'}[0]\to\Lambda_{Z'}[0]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] these are ordinary sheaf endomorphisms; equality of such maps is local since their values on sections glue uniquely. Thus the endomorphisms agree globally. The class restriction used here is the localization compatibility of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], while the exchange restricts to opens by [lem-per-regular-supported-base-change]. If $c=0$, the flag is empty and the class is the canonical identity on its open-and-closed support; the same calculation applies. For empty support all morphisms have zero source.

source.place: XVI Definition 2.3.1, localization of the regular-immersion class

proof.text: Assume $T$ is connected and excellent and fix $x\in T$. If there is no such $x$ the claim is vacuous. Otherwise $T$ is nonempty, as required by [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit]. Put $R_x=\mathcal O_{T,x}$ and $d=\dim R_x$. This is a Noetherian regular local ring, and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] makes its spectrum regular. A regular system of parameters generates its maximal ideal and is a regular sequence of length $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. The residue field is regular (its zero maximal ideal has zero generators), so [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] applies to $i_x$ with codimension $d$. It gives $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}:\Lambda(-d)[-2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_x\Lambda_T$. Unfold the regular pinning construction named in [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit]: ILO XVII Proposition 2.4.1.1 defines the pinning by inverting precisely this Gysin map after localization at $x$. Therefore its value is $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}$. No uniqueness of a potential pinning from its generic value is being assumed. At a generic point $d=0$ and the identity normalization of Gysin gives the identity pinning, as required.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.1.1 (definition of the regular pinning), XVI Theorem 3.1.1

proof.text: For $m\in\mathbf Z$, the twist-and-shift clause of [lem-per-potential-dualizing-regular-unit] constructs the pinning of $\Lambda_T(m)[2m]$ by tensoring the regular pinning with $\Lambda_T(m)$ and shifting by $2m$. Substitute the equality from Step 6 into this specified construction. The resulting pinning is $\operatorname{Cl}_{i_x}^{-1}(m)[2m]$, with target $\Lambda(m-d)[2m-2d]$. The signed twists are locally free lines and their evaluation identifications are canonical by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], so the same substitution applies for negative $m$. This proves the final clause without adding a smoothness or field-of-definition hypothesis.

source.place: XVII Proposition 2.4.1.1 and twist-and-shift of the regular pinnings

Checked the sources in ILO XVI Def 2.2.2.5/2.2.2.7, Prop 2.2.3.1 (compatible with any base change) and Def 2.3.1 (class from the conormal bundle), and XVII Prop 2.4.1.1 (the pinning is the inverse of Cl_i) and Lemma 4.3.1.2. No SGA. The statement is true and is the base-change-plus-pinning delta over absolute-gysin-purity. Edge cases checked: empty Z', c=0, n=1 and n>1, negative m, generic point, identity r, Spec Z_(p) over Z[1/l]. Step 1: the 07C1 hypothesis is checked (finite-type quotient; fibres Noetherian and geometrically regular), and ascent is used twice. Step 2: flat tensor exactness keeps the sequence regular. Step 3: pullback of the Kummer flag composite (pullback D' stays Cartier; intermediate Z_k need not be regular). Step 4: counit compatibility of the exchange plus the adjunction bijection. Step 5: equality reduces to degree-zero endomorphisms, hence is local. Steps 6-7: the regular local chain and the twist clause. C1 fault fixed: the statement asserts that i is a regular immersion with locally constant codimension, and no step proved it. Step 2 now cites lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus (same unit, unsplit, no cycle); uses and proof_deps updated. Accepted as unfolding of the named constructions, which ILO XVI 2.3.1 and XVII 2.4.1.1 make definitions: Cl_i = transpose of eta_{i,n}(-c)[-2c] and pinning = Cl^{-1}, both found only in the proofs of absolute-gysin-purity and regular-unit.
